text.sub: About 1 in 7. A normal share for the last 13 years.
text.tldr: **15.3%** of S&P 500 stocks are climbing (76 of 498): **normal**. A month ago it was 14.5%. SPY closed 3.0% below its record close (Oct 6, 2026) and QQQ 9.1% below its record. Over the last 2 years it is lower than on 72% of days. But it is not rare over the long run: lower than on 77% of days since 2013, and 2023 spent 190 days below it.
text.how: Each S&P 500 stock gets the author's trend check. It counts as **climbing** only if it rises on its own chart **and** beats both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100. The line is the share that does. High = most stocks pull together; low = a few giants carry the index. When the giants sprint ahead, almost nobody can keep up, so the line sinks even while SPY and QQQ climb.
text.cases_note: Look-alike = the first close this low after a long stretch above it, with SPY near its 1-year high. Dip = SPY's lowest close in the next 3 months.
text.data: S&P 500 stocks on the author's setup (own trend, vs the S&P 500, vs the Nasdaq 100), 2005 to Oct 30, 2026. The last 2 years are the radar's own daily numbers (the Market breadth chart below). Before that, today's members are carried back, so stocks that later left the index are missing and older readings can run a little high. SPY and QQQ: daily closes (split-adjusted, no dividends).
